messages:
morgan: Quick snapshot from the weekly privs scan - attached the CSV export, but TL;DR: 42 accounts with admin bindings that haven't acted in 90+ days. Can people triage for obvious service accounts vs. humans? :eyes:

rachel: Thanks, looking now. Do we have KMS key usage logs for the last 90 days for these principals? I want to confirm whether some of them are only key-usage-bound and could stay.

sam: FYI I already tried to correlate with CloudTrail and see a gap for several keys. Might be ingestion delays in the log pipeline for older events.

morgan: @sam which keys specifically? Paste a couple ARNs and I'll include in the postmortem.

sam: Here are two: `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-1111-efgh-2222` and `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/zzzz-9999-xxxx-8888`

taylor: If anyone wants to run a quick lookup, I used this snippet earlier to pull CloudTrail events tied to KMS usage:```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-1111-efgh-2222 --start-time 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2024-12-31T23:59:59Z```

jen: audit-bot just dropped the automated enrichment for the CSV (see link) with last-seen timestamps and whether principal had console/API access. @morgan the enrichment flags 18 of the 42 as 'service' with no recent key usage. :white_check_mark:

audit-bot: Automated report: https://redwood-infra-reports.internal/reports/privs/3678901234 - enriched with last_seen, last_key_use, role_type. (generated 2025-03-18T16:02:00Z)

rachel: For the 18 flagged service accounts — can we map to owning teams? If they belong to legacy infra automation we should open a deprecation CR, not just remove.

morgan: Agreed. Proposed next steps: 1) Sam to confirm KMS log ingestion gap and run replay for the two ARNs, 2) Taylor to map flagged service principals to infra owners, 3) Jen to create a canary removal PR for 10 stale human admins (rollbackable), 4) I will draft a short postmortem for the ingestion gap.

sam: On it — replay started. If CloudTrail replay still missing, I can fallback to S3 raw logs and do a manual parse. ETA 3h.

taylor: I'll ping platform-owners and assemble mapping spreadsheet. Adding fields: owner, slack, last_deploy, suggested action.

jen: I'll open the PR and add an `infrasec:canary` label. Plan: remove grant for 10 least-recently-used humans, wait 48h, monitor error budget and billing metrics.

morgan: Good. One policy ask: can we add a short-lived annotation in KMS key policy before removal so on-call gets an explicit `403` reason if a job fails? Something like `privevent:etag=2025-03-18-3678901234` so we can grep errors.

rachel: That makes sense. We can push a policy patch that denies `kms:Decrypt` with condition `StringEquals` on a temporary tag. Ops will detect and rollback if noise is high.

sam: Replay found events for `abcd-1111` up to 2024-11-02. `zzzz-9999` still shows no usage. I'll attach raw event IDs in the ticket.

morgan: Nice — so `abcd-1111` -> keep, `zzzz-9999` -> candidate for removal pending owner response. I'll create a JIRA and link everything.

taylor: Quick question: do we want to run the least-priv automation (policy-synth) after the canary or before? My vote: after canary so we reduce human risk and then apply machine bindings.

jen: Agreed. Can also use the canary window to collect regressions for the policy-synth test suite.

morgan: OK, I'll assign tickets and circle back in tomorrow's standup. Thanks all :thumbsup:
